Hello! My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm so glad you're here today, and I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you're navigating as a new mother. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool designed to help us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential areas of support you may need during this postpartum period. The EPDS screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable resource in helping us better understand your emotional well-being right now.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe, supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. My goal is to provide you with a non-judgmental and empathetic ear, and to work together to identify any ways we can support you during this time.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions, and we'll take them one at a time. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. Don't worry about "right" or "wrong" answers – this is all about understanding your unique experience and perspective.

So, let's get started. Here's my first question: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. to be honest, it's been really hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to love watching comedies and laughing with my friends, but now it feels like it's just too much effort. I've been so tired all the time, taking care of the baby and trying to keep up with everything, that I just don't seem to have the energy to laugh like I used to. Sometimes my husband will try to make me laugh, and I'll smile, but it's just not the same. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time. There are a few things that still make me smile, like when my baby smiles at me, but it's not like it used to be. I feel like I've lost my sense of humor, and it's really sad for me. (pausing, getting a bit choked up) Sorry, it's just... it's hard to explain. I just don't feel like myself anymore.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) Honestly, no... I haven't been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as I used to. I mean, I'll catch myself smiling when my baby does something cute, but it's not like I'm really laughing or feeling carefree. Most of the time, I'm just worried about something - is the baby eating enough, is the baby sleeping enough, am I doing everything right? It's hard to explain, but it feels like there's this constant weight on my shoulders, and it's hard to shake off. Even when my husband tries to make me laugh, it's just not the same. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? (looking down, fidgeting with hands) I miss feeling happy and carefree, but it's just not something I've been feeling a lot of lately.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head) Not really... I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like too much work. I mean, even simple things like taking a shower or getting dressed feel like huge accomplishments, so planning a fun activity or outing just feels overwhelming. And to be honest, I've been feeling really sad and discouraged a lot of the time, so it's hard to muster up the energy to look forward to things. Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or meeting a friend for coffee, but then I'll just feel anxious about how I'll manage with the baby, or worried that I won't be able to enjoy it because I'll be too tired or preoccupied. (sighing) It's like I've lost my sense of excitement and anticipation, and it's just really hard to find the motivation to do things I used to love. (looking down, voice cracking) It's like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, but I'm not really living.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, looking down) Oh, yeah... I do that a lot. I feel like I'm constantly questioning myself and wondering if I'm doing everything right. If the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not soothing her properly. If she's not sleeping, I think it's because I'm not establishing a good routine. Even when my husband tries to reassure me that I'm doing a great job, I still can't shake the feeling that I'm somehow failing. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I've been feeling really guilty and inadequate as a mother, like I'm just not cut out for this. And it's hard to explain, but it feels like every little thing that goes wrong is my fault, and that I should be able to control everything. (looking up, tears in eyes) It's like I'm walking around with this constant voice in my head, telling me that I'm not good enough, and it's just really hard to silence it. (wiping away a tear) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard to talk about.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, all the time. I worry about everything. Is the baby eating enough? Is the baby sleeping enough? Is the baby healthy? Is the baby safe? (taking a deep breath) I mean, I know it's normal to worry a little bit, but it feels like my mind is constantly racing with worst-case scenarios. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll think, "What if the baby chokes?" or "What if the baby gets sick?" And then I'll start to feel anxious and my heart will start racing, and it's just hard to calm down. (fidgeting with hands) Even when my husband tries to reassure me that everything is fine, I just can't seem to shake the feeling that something is going to go wrong. (looking down) And it's not just about the baby, either. I worry about myself, too. Am I doing enough? Am I a good mother? Am I messing everything up? (sighing) It's just this constant, nagging feeling of anxiety that I don't know how to get rid of. (pausing, looking up) Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? Like, something bad is going to happen, and I just don't know what it is yet. (shaking head) It's exhausting.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, taking a deep breath) Yes, that happens to me too. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like changing the baby's diaper or making lunch, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, my hands will start shaking, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out. (looking down, fidgeting with hands) It's like my body is responding to some kind of threat, but there's no actual threat there. It's just... (pausing, searching for words) ...it's just this feeling of being overwhelmed, I guess. Like, I'm not in control, and everything is just too much for me to handle. (sighing) And it's scary, because I don't know what's triggering it, or how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll try to take some deep breaths, or go for a walk, or talk to my husband, but it's hard to shake the feeling of panic once it's started. (looking up, tears in eyes) It's like I'm losing control, and that's the scariest feeling of all. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I've been having trouble sleeping, too, because I'm always worried about something, and that just makes the anxiety and panic worse. (shaking head) It's a vicious cycle, and I don't know how to break it.
Things have been getting on top of me

(exhaling heavily) Yes, that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I'm constantly worried about whether I'm doing enough, whether the baby is eating enough, sleeping enough, whether I'm meeting all of her needs... (shaking head) And on top of that, I'm trying to manage the household, and take care of myself, and it just feels like too much. (looking down, voice cracking) Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll just start crying because I'm so overwhelmed. (wiping away a tear) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make dinner, and the baby will be crying, and the phone will be ringing, and it's just... (throwing hands up) ...it's too much. I feel like I'm drowning in a sea of responsibility, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (sighing) I just wish someone could take some of the weight off my shoulders, you know? Just for a little while, so I can catch my breath.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Yes, that's me. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping lately. I'll lie awake at night, feeling anxious and overwhelmed, and I just can't seem to shut off my brain. I'll be thinking about all the things I need to do, and all the things that could go wrong, and it's just... (sighing) ...it's exhausting. Even when I do finally fall asleep, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, feeling worried and anxious, and I'll lie there for hours, unable to fall back asleep. (rubbing eyes) And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the fact that I'm so unhappy all the time. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, but I'm not really living. I'm not enjoying the things that I used to enjoy, and I'm not feeling happy or fulfilled. (looking down, voice cracking) It's like I'm just a shell of my former self, and it's really hard to see a way out of this darkness. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Some nights, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll just start crying because I'm so sad and overwhelmed. (wiping away a tear) It's like I'm drowning in my own unhappiness, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears streaming down face) Yes, that's me. I've been feeling so sad and miserable lately. It's like a heavy weight is just sitting on my chest, and I don't know how to lift it off. I'll be doing okay, and then something will happen, and I'll just start crying. It's like the sadness is just beneath the surface, waiting to bubble up at any moment. (sobbing) I feel like I'm grieving the loss of my old life, you know? I'm grieving the loss of my freedom, my independence, my sense of self. I'm grieving the fact that I'm not the same person I used to be. (wiping away tears) And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, you know? I'm supposed to be this happy, glowing new mom, and instead I'm just feeling sad and overwhelmed all the time. (looking down, voice cracking) I feel like I'm failing, like I'm not doing this mom thing right. And it's just... (sighing) ...it's just really hard to deal with. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. I'll think about all the things I used to do, all the things I used to enjoy, and I'll just feel so sad that those things are gone now. (shaking head) It's like I'm living in a fog, and I don't know how to find my way out.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down face) Yes, that's me. I've been crying a lot lately. It's like the sadness and overwhelmed feelings just build up inside me, and then they just overflow in the form of tears. (sobbing) I'll be doing something normal, like changing the baby's diaper or making lunch, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's like I'm not even in control of my emotions anymore. (wiping away tears) Sometimes I'll be crying, and I won't even know why. I'll just be feeling so overwhelmed and sad, and the tears will just start flowing. (shaking head) It's like my emotions are just raw and exposed all the time, and it's really hard to deal with. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I've been crying a lot at night, too, after the baby goes to sleep. I'll just sit there, holding my husband, and crying, because I'm so sad and overwhelmed. (looking down, voice cracking) It's like I'm just barely holding it together, and sometimes the tears are just the only way to release all the emotions that are built up inside me. (sighing) I feel like I'm crying all the time, and it's just... (shaking head) ...it's just really hard to deal with.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking head) No, that's not something I've thought about. I mean, I've felt really overwhelmed and sad, and I've wondered how I'm going to get through all of this, but harming myself has never crossed my mind. (pausing, looking down) I just feel like I'm struggling to cope with everything, and I don't know how to make it better. I feel like I'm just trying to survive each day, and I'm not really living. (sighing) But I would never think about harming myself. I just want to find a way to feel better, to be happy again, and to be a good mom to my baby. (looking up, tears in eyes) I just want to feel like myself again, and I don't know how to get there.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotions and symptoms that are common in the postpartum period, including feelings of sadness, anxiety, and overwhelm. She reports difficulty sleeping, frequent crying spells, and feelings of guilt and worthlessness. The patient's responses suggest a high level of emotional distress and difficulty coping with the demands of motherhood.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 26, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient's response indicates a noticeable decrease in their ability to laugh and see the funny side of things, but not a complete loss, matching the 'Definitely not so much now' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they have lost their sense of excitement and anticipation, and are struggling to find motivation to do things they used to love, matching the 'Hardly at all' option.</sym>, <sym>Patient admits to frequently blaming themselves and feeling guilty, indicating a high level of self-blame, consistent with 'Yes, most of the time</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a high frequency and intensity of feeling scared or panicky for no very good reason, describing it as a wave of panic that happens while doing normal activities, and having trouble shaking the feeling once it starts.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>Patient's response indicates they have been experiencing significant unhappiness and difficulty sleeping, with feelings of anxiety, overwhelm, and sadness, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a strong and frequent feeling of sadness and misery, using phrases such as 'I've been feeling so sad and miserable lately', 'the sadness is just beneath the surface, waiting to bubble up at any moment', and 'I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's EPDS score of 26 indicates a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>. Her symptoms, including <sym>sadness</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, <sym>sleep difficulties</sym>, <sym>guilt</sym>, and <sym>worthlessness</sym>, are consistent with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The patient's denial of suicidal ideation is noted, but her overall presentation suggests a need for urgent referral to a <med>primary care provider</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage patient to reach out to supportive family and friends
3. Recommend <med>sleep hygiene practices</med> to improve sleep quality
4. Suggest <med>relaxation techniques</med>, such as deep breathing or meditation, to manage anxiety and stress
5. Provide patient with resources for <med>postpartum support groups</med> and <med>online mental health resources</med>
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 26: **Postpartum Depression Screening Summary**

The patient presents with several symptoms and emotional/behavioral concerns that warrant further evaluation. The main symptoms expressed include:

* Persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and enjoyment in activities
* Difficulty coping with daily responsibilities and caring for her baby
* Anxiety, worry, and feelings of being overwhelmed
* Sleep difficulties, including trouble falling asleep and staying asleep due to anxiety and worry
* Frequent crying spells and feelings of guilt and worthlessness

Consistent patterns across answers include:

* Low mood and loss of enjoyment in activities
* Anxiety and worry about the baby's health and well-being
* Difficulty coping with the demands of motherhood
* Feelings of guilt and worthlessness

Potential areas of screening significance relevant to postpartum depression or anxiety include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of worthlessness or guilt
* Anxiety, panic, or being overwhelmed

Specific risk factors identified include:

* Persistent sadness and crying spells
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Anxiety and panic symptoms, including feelings of being overwhelmed

It is noted that the patient denied any thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation.

**Screening Observation Summary:**

The patient's responses suggest a high level of emotional distress and difficulty coping with the demands of motherhood. The presence of persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, anxiety, and sleep difficulties warrants further evaluation for potential postpartum depression or anxiety. The patient's feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and being overwhelmed also require attention. While the patient denied any thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation, her overall presentation suggests a need for ongoing support and monitoring. Further assessment and evaluation are recommended to determine the best course of action for supporting the patient's mental health and well-being.
